25.explanation: The G7 began (as the G6 at Rambouillet, 1975) to coordinate responses to the oil shock and financial instability of the 1970s.

26.explanation: The G7 members are the US, UK, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and Canada (with the EU taking part). Australia is not a member.

27.explanation: The IORA Secretariat is in Mauritius (Ebene, near Port Louis).

28.explanation: 'Global South' means developing and emerging economies. It is a political-economic term, not a strictly geographic one.

29.explanation: At the Évian outreach session (16 June 2026) Modi said the world's biggest challenge is not a lack of resources but a growing deficit of trust.

sources.title: The Statesman: Trust deficit, not resource scarcity, biggest challenge – Modi at G7

30.explanation: Nehru and Ayub Khan signed the Indus Waters Treaty in Karachi on 19 September 1960, with the World Bank as broker.

31.explanation: The PCA (The Hague, 1899) is an independent intergovernmental organisation, not a UN organ.

32.explanation: The Ratle project is on the Chenab. Kishenganga is on the Kishenganga (Neelum), a Jhelum tributary.

33.explanation: A transboundary river flows across the territory of more than one sovereign state.

34.explanation: The Sutlej rises near Lake Rakshastal in Tibet. The Ravi, Beas and Chenab rise in Himachal Pradesh.

35.explanation: Pondage is the limited storage a run-of-river plant may keep, so the dispute is about reservoir storage regulation under the Treaty.

36.explanation: The 36th Amendment Act, 1975 made Sikkim a full State. The 35th (1974) had made it an 'associate state'.

37.explanation: Under the 1950 Indo-Sikkim Treaty Sikkim was an Indian protectorate (briefly an associate state in 1974–75). It was never a UT, a Part B State or a Portuguese colony.

38.explanation: Nathu La links Sikkim with Tibet. Zoji La is in Ladakh/J&K, Shipki La in HP and Lipulekh in Uttarakhand.

39.explanation: All three are correct. Sikkim alone borders China, Nepal and Bhutan; Khangchendzonga NP (2016) is India's first mixed World Heritage Site; and Kangchenjunga is the highest peak within India's administered territory.

40.explanation: The 1890 Convention of Calcutta (Britain–China) fixed the Sikkim–Tibet boundary and recognised Britain's protectorate over Sikkim.

41.explanation: The Kalapani–Limpiyadhura dispute turns on how the Sugauli Treaty (1815–16) defines the source of the Kali river.

42.explanation: The Jaynagar–Kurtha line runs from Jaynagar in Bihar to Janakpur/Kurtha in Nepal.

43.explanation: Nepal borders only India and China (Tibet). Bhutan is separated from it by Sikkim.

44.explanation: BIMSTEC and BBIN are seen as sub-regional alternatives that get around SAARC's paralysis.

45.explanation: Linking UPI with Nepal's National Payments Interface (NPI) enables cross-border P2P payments and remittances.

46.explanation: The Pancheshwar Multipurpose Project is on the Mahakali under the 1996 Mahakali Treaty.

47.explanation: The Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT compiles and releases the WPI, including the new 2022–23 series.

48.explanation: A PPI measures prices producers receive. The CPI measures prices consumers pay.

49.explanation: The WPI tracks wholesale-stage prices. The other pairs are mismatched.

50.explanation: The first-phase Service PPI covers banking, securities transactions, insurance, pension fund management, railways, air (passenger) and telecom. Port trust charges and warehousing are not included.

51.explanation: The move to PPIs follows IMF guidance (the PPI Manual and SDDS standards) on producer-price statistics.

52.explanation: Gross Value of Output is a national income accounting concept (output weights for GVA/PPI).
